deep.reconstruction: There is no mathematics on this page. It is a fair copy, in German Kurrent script, of a lesson in ancient Greek history. It continues the account begun on fol. 107 of Epaminondas' last Peloponnesian campaign. Content, in order: (1) The Thebans break into Sparta itself but are driven back. (2) Epaminondas immediately turns back to seize Mantinea. A body ('Chor') of Athenian troops reaches the city before him, so he camps outside the walls to await the Spartans. (3) The Spartan army is nearly as strong as his own (30,000 men). (4) On '27 Juni' a memorable battle takes place. An interlinear insertion above the date appears to read '36? J.' (a year, probably 362/363 B.C.). (5) The battle lasts almost the whole day without a decision. (6) Epaminondas finally places himself at the head of the 'h. Schaar' (presumably 'heilige Schaar', the Theban Sacred Band), breaks into the Spartan ranks and cuts a path. He is then surrounded by the mass of enemies and struck by a weapon. The sentence continues on fol. 109 with '...durchbohrte ihm die Brust'. This is the standard school narrative of the Battle of Mantinea, 362 B.C., as found in Xenophon, Diodorus and Plutarch. The neat, regular hand and the schoolbook content suggest a pupil's history notebook bound into the bundle, not Gauss's own working notes; this is an inference from the hand, not a verified attribution. Nothing is derived or computed.
errors: Historical, not mathematical: the Battle of Mantinea is usually dated to 362 B.C. (Olympiad 104.3, summer). A year of 363 in the insertion would be off by one. The previous page itself gives '362 vor Chr.'.
The precise date '27 Juni' is not securely attested in ancient sources. Modern equivalents are conjectural; Boeckh-style reckonings give a date around early July 362.
